lines: Come on — everybody's doing it. That whispered message, half **invitation** and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure. It usually leads to no good — drinking, drugs and casual sex. But in her new book Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure, in which organizations and officials use the power of group dynamics to help individuals improve their lives and possibly the world.
“来吧——大家都这么做。”这种半是**邀请**、半是强制的耳语，是我们大多数人听到“同辈压力”一词时会想到的东西。它通常引向不良后果——酗酒、吸毒和滥交。但蒂娜·罗森伯格在新书《加入俱乐部》中提出，同辈压力也可以成为一种积极的力量，途径就是她所称的“社会治疗”：组织和官员们利用群体动力的力量，帮助个人改善自己的生活，甚至可能改变世界。

lines: Rosenberg, the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize, offers a host of examples of the social cure in action: In South Carolina, a state-sponsored antismoking program called Rage Against the Haze sets out to make cigarettes uncool. lines: The idea seems promising, and Rosenberg is a perceptive observer. Her critique of the **lameness** of many public-health campaigns is spot-on: they fail to mobilize peer pressure for healthy habits, and they demonstrate a seriously flawed understanding of psychology. "Dare to be different, please don't smoke!" pleads one billboard campaign aimed at reducing smoking among teenagers — teenagers who desire nothing more than fitting in. Rosenberg argues **convincingly** that public-health advocates ought to take a page from advertisers, so skilled at applying peer pressure.
这个想法似乎很有前景，而罗森伯格也是一位敏锐的观察者。她对许多公共卫生宣传活动效果不佳的批评十分中肯：这些活动未能利用同辈压力来促进健康习惯，也暴露出对心理学的严重误解。一项旨在减少青少年吸烟的广告牌宣传恳求道：“敢于与众不同，请不要吸烟！”——可青少年最渴望的恰恰是融入同伴。罗森伯格令人信服地指出，公共卫生倡导者应该向那些极善于运用同辈压力的广告商学习。

lines: But on the general effectiveness of the social cure, Rosenberg is less persuasive. Join the Club is filled with too much irrelevant detail and not enough exploration of the social and biological factors that make peer pressure so powerful. The most glaring flaw of the social cure as it's presented here is that it doesn't work very well for very long. Rage Against the Haze failed once state funding was cut. Evidence that the loveLife program produces lasting changes is limited and **mixed**.

lines: There's no doubt that our peer groups exert enormous influence on our behavior. An emerging body of research shows that positive health habits — as well as negative ones — spread through networks of friends via social communication. This is a subtle form of peer pressure: we **unconsciously** imitate the behavior we see every day.
毫无疑问，同辈群体对我们的行为有着巨大的影响。越来越多的研究表明，积极的健康习惯和消极的健康习惯一样，都会通过社交在朋友圈网络中传播。这是同辈压力的一种微妙形式：我们会**不自觉地**模仿每天看到的行为。

lines: Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select our peer groups and steer their activities in virtuous directions. It's like the teacher who breaks up the troublemakers in the back row by pairing them with better-behaved classmates. The tactic never really works. And that's the problem with a social cure **engineered** from the outside: in the real world, as in school, we insist on choosing our own friends.
然而，远不能确定的是，专家和官僚们究竟有多大本事为我们的同辈群体把关，并引导他们的活动向善。这就像老师把后排捣乱的学生拆开，让他们与表现较好的同学同桌。这种策略从来没有真正奏效过。而这正是从外部**策划**的“社会治疗”的问题所在：在现实世界中，就像在学校里一样，我们坚持自己选择朋友。

lines: The conflict has been surfacing since 2002, when the corporation bought Vermont's only nuclear power plant, an aging reactor in Vernon. As a condition of receiving state approval for the sale, the company agreed to seek permission from state regulators to operate past 2012. In 2006, the state went a step further, requiring that any extension of the plant's license be subject to the Vermont legislature's approval. Then, too, the company went along.
这一冲突自2002年起便已浮现：当年该公司买下了佛蒙特州唯一的核电站——位于弗农的一座日渐老化的反应堆。作为州政府批准该交易的条件，公司同意就2012年之后的运行向州监管机构申请许可。2006年，州政府更进一步，要求该核电站许可证的任何延期都必须得到佛蒙特州议会的批准。当时公司也同样表示了同意。

lines: Either Entergy never really intended to live by those commitments, or it simply didn't foresee what would happen next. A string of accidents, including the partial collapse of a cooling tower in 2007 and the discovery of an underground pipe system **leakage**, raised serious questions about both Vermont Yankee's safety and Entergy's management — especially after the company made misleading statements about the pipe. Enraged by Entergy's behavior, the Vermont Senate voted 26 to 4 last year against allowing an extension.

lines: Now the company is suddenly claiming that the 2002 agreement is invalid because of the 2006 legislation, and that only the federal government has regulatory power over nuclear issues. lines: In the idealized version of how science is done, facts about the world are waiting to be observed and collected by objective researchers who use the scientific method to carry out their work. But in the everyday practice of science, discovery frequently follows an ambiguous and complicated route. We aim to be objective, but we cannot escape the context of our unique life experiences. lines: Consequently, discovery claims should be thought of as **protoscience**. Similar to newly staked mining claims, they are full of potential. lines: Once a discovery claim becomes public, the discoverer receives intellectual credit. But, unlike with mining claims, the community takes control of what happens next. Within the complex social structure of the scientific community, researchers make discoveries; editors and reviewers act as **gatekeepers** by controlling the publication process; other scientists use the new finding to suit their own purposes; and finally, the public (including other scientists) receives the new discovery and possibly accompanying technology. As a discovery claim works its way through the community, the interaction and confrontation between shared and competing beliefs about the science and the technology involved transforms an individual's discovery claim into the community's credible discovery.

一旦发现声明公之于众，发现者便获得知识的声誉。但与采矿权不同，接下来发生的事情便由科学共同体掌控。在科学界复杂的社会结构中，研究者作出发现；编辑和审稿人通过控制发表过程充当**守门人**；其他科学家则按自己的目的利用这一新发现；最后，公众（包括其他科学家）接受这项新发现以及可能随之而来的技术。当发现声明在科学界层层流转时，围绕相关科学技术的共识与分歧之间的互动和碰撞，便把个人的发现声明转化为科学共同体认可的可信发现。

lines: Two paradoxes exist throughout this credibility process. First, scientific work tends to focus on some aspect of prevailing knowledge that is viewed as incomplete or incorrect. Little reward accompanies duplication and confirmation of what is already known and believed. The goal is new-search, not re-search. Not surprisingly, newly published discovery claims and credible discoveries that appear to be important and convincing will always be open to challenge and potential modification or **refutation** by future researchers. Second, novelty itself frequently provokes disbelief. Nobel Laureate and physiologist Albert Szent-Gyorgyi once described discovery as "seeing what everybody has seen and thinking what nobody has thought." But thinking what nobody else has thought and telling others what they have missed may not change their views. Sometimes years are required for truly novel discovery claims to be accepted and appreciated.

在这一可信性认证过程中始终存在两个悖论。其一，科学工作往往聚焦于公认知识中被视为不完整或不正确的某个方面。重复和确认人们已经知晓并相信的东西几乎得不到什么回报。目标是new-search（新探索），而非re-search（重复研究）。不出所料，新近发表的重要且令人信服的发现声明和可信发现，将始终面对后来研究者的挑战以及可能的修正或**驳斥**。其二，新颖本身常常招致怀疑。诺贝尔奖得主、生理学家圣捷尔吉曾把发现描述为“看见每个人都看见过的，想到没有人想到过的”。但想到别人没想到的、告诉别人他们错过了什么，未必能改变他们的看法。真正新颖的发现声明有时需要多年才能被接受和赏识。

lines: If the trade unionist Jimmy Hoffa were alive today, he would probably represent civil servants. lines: This tendency in the natural sciences has long been evident in the social sciences too. (47) Here, Darwinism seems to offer justification, for if all humans share common origins, it seems reasonable to suppose that cultural diversity could also be traced to more constrained beginnings. Just as the bewildering variety of human courtship rituals might all be considered forms of sexual selection, perhaps the world's languages, music, social and religious customs and even history are governed by universal features. (48) To filter out what is unique from what is shared might enable us to understand how complex cultural behavior arose and what guides it in evolutionary or cognitive terms.

自然科学的这一倾向，也早已在社会科学中显现。(47) 在这一点上，达尔文主义似乎给出了理论依据：因为如果全人类拥有共同的起源，那么认为文化的多样性同样可以追溯到某些更为有限的源头，似乎也是合理的。正如人类形形色色的求爱仪式或许都可以视为性选择的形式，世界上的语言、音乐、社会与宗教习俗，乃至历史，或许也受到普遍特征的支配。(48) 从共性中过滤出特性，或许能使我们理解复杂的文化行为是如何产生的，以及在进化或认知层面上是什么在引导它。

lines: The most famous of these efforts was initiated by Noam Chomsky, who suggested that humans are born with an innate language-acquisition capacity that dictates a universal grammar. A few generative rules are then sufficient to unfold the entire fundamental structure of a language, which is why children can learn it so quickly. (49) The second, by Joshua Greenberg, takes a more empirical approach to universality, identifying traits (particularly in word order) shared by many languages, which are considered to represent biases that result from cognitive constraints.
这些努力中最著名的一次是由诺姆·乔姆斯基开创的，他提出，人类天生具有一种决定着普遍语法的语言习得能力。只需少数几条生成规则，便足以展开一种语言的整个基本结构，这正是儿童能如此迅速学会语言的原因。(49) 第二次尝试由约书亚·格林伯格作出，他以更重经验的方法来考察普遍性：鉴别出许多语言共有的特征（尤其在词序方面），这些特征被认为是认知制约所导致的偏向的体现。

lines: Gray and his colleagues have put them to the test by examining four family trees that between them represent more than 2,000 languages. sample: The cartoon vividly illustrates the difference between an **optimistic** and a **pessimistic** attitude towards the same setback. What has happened cannot be undone; the only thing we can choose is how to respond. The pessimist fixates on what is lost and allows frustration to paralyze him, while the optimist focuses on what remains and turns misfortune into a starting point. As an old saying goes, when one door closes, another opens. Life never lacks setbacks, but it always offers possibilities to those willing to look for them.

sample: In my view, optimism is not naive self-comfort but a **prerequisite** of success. Countless great figures, from scientists to entrepreneurs, stumbled badly before they succeeded, and it was their hopeful outlook that carried them through.
